- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–2% for 30d forecasts.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day post-spike.
- If official event net supply is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment oscillates; if forecast is trending upward with mixed sentiment, cap slope at 0.1–0.3% per day.
- When official events are frequent (≥20/30d) and supply net is negative, model tends to underestimate volatility; increase forecast variance by 0.5–1.0% for risk-adjusted output.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted moving average (e.g., 7-day) to smooth forecast trajectory.
